name: Resume builders
intro: Where the PDF exports clean with no paywall, and where they hold your finished resume hostage.

apps.title: Kickresume: AI Resume Builder
apps.verdict: The best templates in this category by far: unconventional layouts that stand out from generic ATS-friendly one-pagers, making them a solid pick for creative and design-oriented fields. The AI assistant rewrites job descriptions into cleaner, sharper language. The mobile experience is noticeably weaker than the web: crashes during editing, no back button, and preview is thumbnail-only.
apps.loved: A wide range of distinctive templates plus an AI rephrasing tool for experience descriptions both tools genuinely speed up writing.
apps.weak: The mobile editor crashes when typing in the experience field, there is no full-size document preview, and there is no back button.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants a template that does not look like everyone else's and is comfortable finishing the resume on a desktop.

quotes.text: Love how it helps me rewrite my cover letter to be more succinct and the unique layouts are great. I do wish that the bugs were fixed when having the AI assist. It cuts off paragraphs mid thought, so you have to start it over from scratch. Also, there's no go back button.

apps.title: Got Resume Builder
apps.verdict: One of the few apps in this space where export actually works without a mandatory subscription. The interface is minimal: font changes and page layout options are available for free. The downside is that templates are very basic with no color customization or block reordering. No cover letter.
apps.loved: Free PDF and email export with no hidden charges, quick editing for a specific job opening, and data that persists between sessions.
apps.weak: Templates are minimal and cannot be customized by color or section order. No cover letter. Word export is weak.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants a working PDF fast, without signing up or paying extra.

quotes.text: I really like this app, but after spending almost an hour getting my resume together I cannot save it. When I send it as an email it doesn't send anything.

apps.title: Resume Builder⁺
apps.verdict: A simple builder with no unnecessary clutter. Gets the job done for a quick task, but is very limited: only one free template, no option to import an existing resume, and no landscape orientation support. The cover letter feature is mentioned but not fleshed out.
apps.loved: A resume comes together in minutes with no sign-up needed the step-by-step input keeps you focused and avoids choice overload.
apps.weak: Only one free template, no import of an existing document, and sharing or downloading the file requires a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Someone with no resume-writing experience who needs a first draft right now, from their phone.

apps.title: Resume Builder - CV Engineer
apps.verdict: A lightweight editor with a sensible structure and clean, watermark-free templates. Two free exports is a fair threshold. The AI rephrasing feature is available as a paid add-on and is not pushed aggressively. The weak point is rigid bullet formatting in the experience section that cannot be removed or reformatted.
apps.loved: Templates without watermarks, actual employer callbacks noted by several users, and fast updates for a specific role.
apps.weak: Forced bullet points in the experience section cannot be turned off, section titles cannot be changed, no cover letter.
apps.whoFor: Someone who needs to update their resume quickly for a new role without fiddling with settings.

quotes.text: Went through and made the entire resume thinking oh yea the tools are what you pay for with the plan no it's actually the download ability is what you pay for plus the tools

Only 2 free downloads. Make sure it doesn't glitch and remove anything before downloading. My first one cleared a whole description for one of my work history. Otherwise very easy to use. Very simple templates so don't expect fancy and best part no watermark!

apps.title: Resume AI – Intelligent CV App
apps.verdict: The AI assistant builds resume sections through a Q&A flow. Importing an existing resume is destructive: it collapses job titles into generic versions and drops details. The coin-based monetization layered on top of a subscription frustrates users who are already paying.
apps.loved: The Q&A format lowers the barrier for people who do not know where to start, and produces a result in about 5 minutes.
apps.weak: Importing a resume overwrites original job titles with generic placeholders. Academic CV format (long-form) is not supported.
apps.whoFor: A job seeker writing their first resume who needs guidance on what to include.

quotes.text: I used the option to import an existing version and the output... It had removed ALL the detail and reduced the length of job titles to generic versions and what's more gave ratings out of 5 for each skill

Downloaded the app to help me make a professional CV for academia. This is not a resume. CV and resumes are NOT the same. The app says helps with CV's it does NOT it will write a one or two page resume but my whole career and body of work displayed on a CV is missing.

apps.title: Resume Builder by Nobody
apps.verdict: One of the few builders where the paid version is a one-time purchase, not a subscription. Templates are minimal and ATS-friendly by default. The weak point is chronological ordering: new entries are added to the bottom of the list instead of the top, which breaks the standard reverse-chronological format.
apps.loved: Build a resume without creating an account data lives locally, so you can finish and leave without friction.
apps.weak: New experience entries are appended to the end of the list, not the top reverse chronological order does not hold automatically and has to be fixed manually.
apps.whoFor: Someone who needs a clean, single-page document without decorations, in a format that works for standard job boards or PDF submission.

quotes.text: I purchased this app to create my résumé which I did two years ago I've now got more jobs to add to my résumé however when you add a new job it puts in at the bottom instead of at the top. A résumé is supposed to be from your most recent job onward

apps.title: Resume Builder - AI Resumate
apps.verdict: An AI editor with a clean fill-in flow. The core mechanic AI automatically rephrasing your entered experience is appreciated by most users, but some lose nuances from the original. Export is hidden behind a paywall in a way that is not obvious: users find out only after filling everything in.
apps.loved: Fast to fill out and easy to edit after saving.
apps.weak: AI sometimes replaces specific wording with generic phrases and there is no way to undo it. The download button does not work for some users even after payment.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants AI to improve their wording and is willing to review the result before sending.

quotes.text: The ai changes everything to something. Completely different

apps.title: Resume Builder Pro with AI
apps.verdict: AI suggestions while editing text work and are valued, but PDF export is systemically broken the resume disappears or fails to open after generation. The font in print view shifts, and capitalization changes on its own. Not reliable for the core task of downloading and sending.
apps.loved: AI rewrites and improves job responsibility text right in the editor users say it speeds up the process.
apps.weak: PDF export is unstable: the file does not save, fonts and capitalization shift in print view, and support is unreachable.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants help with wording but is prepared to run the final document through a different tool to actually get the file.

quotes.text: I've built a resume and selected download. I get a 'generating PDF' but the resume disappears. It's not in my files folder. I've already paid for the app and wish I didn't.

The résumé looks beautiful online, but when I printed out the wording is weird, the letters aren't the same size some letters are uppercase when they shouldn't be. It literally looks like an AI mess up.

apps.title: Resume Star 2: Pro CV Designer
apps.verdict: The app bills itself as free and actually delivers on that no payment required. But Dropbox and iCloud sync is unreliable: data is lost when switching between devices. The PDF sometimes gets rejected by job sites.
apps.loved: Genuinely free export, fast to fill in, clean interface.
apps.weak: Cloud sync drops data when switching between iPhone and iPad. Editing an existing resume is non-obvious users end up creating a new one instead of updating the old one.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants a resume without paying and does not plan to switch devices frequently.

quotes.text: The app says that the resumes are formatted as PDF's, but job sites will never accept the app. They always say 'invalid format'. Then I can't send the resume to my email to forward to anyone.
The app says that the resumes are formatted as PDF's, but job sites will never accept the app. They always say 'invalid format'.

apps.title: Resume Designer 3
apps.verdict: A long-running app aimed at users without a computer. Template fill-in is fast and the PDF output is clean. The consistent weak point is export reliability: email attachments arrive empty, uploading to Monster requires a separate registration, and direct upload to third-party platforms is not available. Saving an edited template as a new file is not possible.
apps.loved: The simplest flow possible: pick a template, fill in fields, print. Gets the job done for anyone who needs a paper resume.
apps.weak: Email attachments arrive empty the resume is lost after filling in. Direct file upload to job sites without going through Monster registration is not available. An edited template cannot be saved as a separate file.
apps.whoFor: A candidate applying for roles that accept paper or printed resumes and are not screened by ATS.

quotes.text: I already paid for this app they're trying to make me pay for it again and leaving watermarks on my resume now
Advertised as free, but not even a free trial, you have to pay to remove watermark. Don't bother

apps.title: Resume : Intelligent CV Maker
apps.verdict: The app is functionally straightforward: templates exist, the editor works, and it is enough for a quick CV. But subscription management is broken several users cannot cancel, and charges keep coming. In the free version, ads cover the entire screen.
apps.loved: No extra steps: pick a template, fill in sections, get a PDF the path is not confusing.
apps.weak: The subscription cannot be canceled through the app's standard interface. Ads cover the full screen and cannot be dismissed.
apps.whoFor: A user who needs a basic PDF once and does not want a subscription though that is not guaranteed here.

quotes.text: Add An Option To Change the text colour their is only colour change option for the heading but not for the body which make it looks dull faded and light and make the document look unprofessional by this the chances for rejection increases so update it with the necessary changes.

apps.title: Resume Star: Pro CV Maker
apps.verdict: A simple CV editor with an approachable interface, but with a critical flaw: the export and send function often fails entirely emails do not go out and the send button is inactive. Several users have lost their resume with no way to recover it. Positioned for the UK market (CV format with photo and personal details), but the templates do not fully match that format.
apps.loved: The interface needs no learning curve a first-time resume writer can manage independently, the steps are obvious.
apps.weak: The built-in CV email function does not work for a significant portion of users. Data is lost without warning.
apps.whoFor: A user without a laptop who needs to build a CV entirely on their phone assuming export works.

quotes.text: Took my money twice in purchasing and CANNOT even email my cv load of rubbish, and trying to contact your support is OUT OF THE QUESTION as when trying to email you guys to show you the screenshots of the problems, apparently the SEND option is not even working

apps.title: Resume & CV Builder
apps.verdict: A simple form editor with basic templates. The key pain point is that switching templates wipes all entered data, and sections cannot be manually reordered. Export is locked behind a paywall.
apps.loved: Fills out quickly and the result looks professional on the first attempt.
apps.weak: Work experience entries cannot be reordered without deleting and re-entering them. Switching templates deletes all your data.
apps.whoFor: Someone who updates their resume once every few years and does not want to deal with settings.

quotes.text: Used resume app for years. What would be helpful is if you could rearrange your work history. When you enter new work experience, it adds it to the bottom of the list. And if you like to have your most recent/relevant work experience at the top you have to delete each job you've had and start from s
Go to change the template and guess what everything all my information goes away besides that I can't figure out how I can share the résumé with the companies that are waiting for my résumé.

Going through templates and they do not include all the information I entered. Each template is missing either my name or my job experience. Doesn't really make sense to use this app if all of your information cannot be displayed on template fo your choosing

apps.title: Quick Resume Pro
apps.verdict: The app has been around for years and has built a loyal user base among people without computers. The template selection is broad and mostly free. The main systemic problem is that experience entries cannot be sorted by date the app lists them in the order they were entered, which breaks chronological ordering. This is not a UI bug but a missing sort feature.
apps.loved: Most templates are free. Acts as a computer substitute for people who do not have one. Quick start without registration.
apps.weak: Experience entries cannot be reordered, so the resume ends up with broken chronology. Backspace in a description field sometimes deletes the entire paragraph. A review prompt pop-up blocks access to the resume and cannot be closed.
apps.whoFor: Someone without a laptop who needs a basic resume for a job application with no ATS or design requirements.

quotes.text: I like the app but it's kind of hard to edit after you submit and the resume is complete. I cant seem to put in order my job experiences and when I sent it to a recruiter they told me the organization of the resume is what caused me to lose the position I was applying for.

apps.title: Resume Creator AI, PDF Builder
apps.verdict: The app offers clean templates and a straightforward fill-in flow but hits a dead end at export: PDF is subscription-only, and the subscription is often impossible to cancel through the standard iOS interface. No import for an existing CV everything is entered from scratch. Sections for awards and references are missing.
apps.loved: The interface is self-explanatory. Templates are reportedly tailored to specific industries, according to at least one user.
apps.weak: No import for an existing resume a long CV has to be typed in manually. PDF export is locked until you subscribe, and that subscription is hard to cancel through iOS settings. No section for awards or references.
apps.whoFor: An entry-level applicant with a short work history who does not need to import anything and is fine with a basic set of sections.

quotes.text: they hold your resume hostage until you pay for a subscription. After arduously creating a profile and typing everything out I was unable to export without paying for a subscription. Additionally you cannot screenshot without the entire resume disappearing.
I wasted my time filling in the information only for the application to fail to generate my CV into either PDF or word document.
So the app doesn't have the option to upload a CV. Which means if you have a 10 page CV like mine you have to renter it one digit at a time! This is painful so I didn't do it.

apps.title: Resume Builder: PDF Resume App
apps.verdict: The web version works well and produces clean templates, but the mobile app is a separate product with systemic crashes: trying to open or save a resume closes the app and loses progress. For the mobile audience it is effectively unusable.
apps.loved: Templates are clean and readable, the input structure is straightforward, and the fill-in process raises no questions.
apps.weak: The mobile app crashes when opening a saved resume or saving new data progress is lost without warning.
apps.whoFor: A user who works through a browser on a computer and just wants to download a PDF.

apps.title: Resume Builder - PDF Templates
apps.verdict: The app works as a builder, but aggressive ads interrupt editing throughout. Paid template credits do not always unlock after purchase. Canceling a subscription is a problem several reviews describe continued charges after cancellation.
apps.loved: Fast data entry in a single form, a finished template in 10 to 15 minutes.
apps.weak: Ads pop up with every field transition. A paid credit is deducted but the template does not unlock. Skill and section order cannot be customized.
apps.whoFor: Someone willing to put up with ads for a quick basic result and who has no plans to pay for templates.

quotes.text: I wish there were more options to allow more of custom attributes such as changing the color options. It would also be cool if you could move the sections around while in preview mode. And lose the restrictions on margin size and font size.

apps.title: Resume Maker⁺
apps.verdict: The step-by-step wizard makes it easier to structure a CV, but it hits a wall at export: PDF is either completely broken or requires payment that is not disclosed until after all fields are filled in. Template formatting breaks in some layouts content is cut off on the right edge and spacing cannot be adjusted. The cover letter generator produces a shifted layout.
apps.loved: Step-by-step input reduces stress for users who do not know resume structure. Templates are visually appealing.
apps.weak: PDF does not generate after filling in the button freezes. Editing an already-created resume is blocked. Several templates in the set clip content on the right side, making them effectively unusable.
apps.whoFor: A user who wants structural guidance for their CV but is not willing to pay for the output file.

quotes.text: Let's me get all the way to the end of making the resume just to never load after pressing the 'generate pdf' button.
One cover letter generation was off center with the right side of the page cut off. The template designs are ok but don't utilize the space well

apps.title: Professional Resume Builder
apps.verdict: The editor offers voice input and a few basic templates, but export is locked behind a paywall with no warning until the very end. Experience sections cannot be sorted and blocks cannot be moved. Template designs are closer to the Word 95 era.
apps.loved: Voice input speeds up text entry. The interface is simple enough for users with no Word experience.
apps.weak: PDF export is hidden behind a paywall that only appears after the entire resume is filled in. Experience entry order is fixed and cannot be changed. Templates are outdated and cannot be structurally edited.
apps.whoFor: Someone without a computer who needs to put together a basic resume once, quickly, with no design expectations.

quotes.text: stay away from this junk, they want 50 bucks to release the resume you spent an hour typing up...

apps.title: Resume Builder & CV Maker AI
apps.verdict: Functionally broken for actual use: sections cannot be reordered, data is deleted on exit, LinkedIn import drops key fields, and aggressive upsell pop-ups appear every 6 seconds. AI features are advertised but inactive for some users. The weakest product in this roundup by actual quality.
apps.loved: LinkedIn profile import is formally available and speeds up initial setup when the data does not get lost.
apps.weak: Resume sections cannot be moved. Data is deleted without warning. Upgrade prompts appear every few seconds and block the editing interface.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state.

quotes.text: I was finishing my cover letter and the app deleted my whole profile. I'm so mad as I took my time with my profile
Really limited editing, can't move sections to where you want them. Doesn't feel worth £8 a week.
Not able to adjust, edit add text. Misses many important fields while importing LinkedIn profile. Not for professionals

apps.title: Resume AI - CV Maker & Builder
apps.verdict: The app generates a CV through AI, but users who left substantive reviews note that the generated text cannot be meaningfully edited, and downloading the finished document causes problems. The actual product experience is almost invisible behind a layer of identical five-star ratings.
apps.loved: AI handles the initial draft, which lowers the barrier for people who do not know how to phrase their experience.
apps.weak: AI-generated wording cannot be edited at a granular level after generation. Export is unstable. The review sample is too small and uniform to draw reliable conclusions about actual quality.
apps.whoFor: Someone who has never written a resume and wants to get something down quickly without worrying about the details.

apps.title: Resume Maker Professional
apps.verdict: The app deletes entered data on its own when navigating between sections. PDF export is locked behind a subscription that some users get billed for immediately on first launch, without explicit consent. The Send button does not work after payment goes through.
apps.loved: Clear section structure, templates with phrasing hints.
apps.weak: Data auto-deletes when returning to previous sections. Subscription charges appear on first launch without explicit consent. PDF is not accessible without payment, and payment does not always activate the feature.
apps.whoFor: Not relevant basic data saving does not work reliably.

quotes.text: the app was not only self deleting sections of the resume i had previously completed but when you're all done typing out your cover letter and your resume you find out you can't even use it unless you give th

apps.title: CV Resume
apps.verdict: Templates are locked until payment, custom sections cannot be added, and template previews are unavailable. The app effectively just collects your data and then demands payment at the final step.
apps.loved: Nothing specific could be identified from the reviews.
apps.weak: Templates cannot be previewed before selection. Custom sections are not available. The interface does not respond to taps in several scenarios.
apps.whoFor: Not relevant the app does not fulfill the basic function of a resume builder.

apps.title: CV Maker ·
apps.verdict: A cover letter and resume editor with a critical save problem: when moving between fields, text reverts to the placeholder example. Users have rewritten their content 12 to 20 times with no success. Export crashes the app.
apps.loved: Visually appealing templates.
apps.weak: Text in fields reverts to the placeholder when moving to the next screen. Export closes the app without saving. The Next button disappears mid-flow.
apps.whoFor: Not relevant the app does not allow the finished document to be saved.

quotes.text: I spent over an hour trying to write my cover letter, and once I was completed it erased everything I wrote and reverted back to the example text.

I downloaded and payed for the subscription so I could make a cover letter with ease and minimum issues but I got the exact opposite. I had to redo my cover letter about 12 times, because the information wouldn't save or would go back to the original text that they give you.

scenarios.name: First job and fresh graduates
scenarios.job: Need a first resume from scratch, fast and without knowing the structure. This also covers people who haven’t written a resume in years and are back on the job market.
scenarios.gap: Someone writing a first resume is helped by questions about their experience and by examples of what to fill in. An AI edit has to keep the original meaning and have an undo.

scenarios.name: Experienced job seekers updating a resume
scenarios.job: They already have a working resume or a LinkedIn profile and need to update it quickly for a new role, add the latest job or shift the emphasis. They don’t want to rebuild it from scratch.
scenarios.gap: In the reviews the import skips fields, and a new job ends up somewhere other than expected. What is needed is a check on the data that carried over and manual control of the order.

scenarios.name: Job seekers who work from a phone only
scenarios.job: Create or update a resume on a phone, save it and send it to an employer without a computer.
scenarios.gap: Authors describe an empty attachment and sending that doesn’t work. What is needed is an independent way to save the file and open it through the system share sheet.

scenarios.name: Professionals with ATS and design requirements
scenarios.job: Prepare a document to the requirements of a particular posting, and check the layout, the content and the export format.
scenarios.gap: In the reviews people ask for a long CV and extended sections. It helps to test a multi-page document, the publications and the exported result, while keeping manual settings.
